terms.definition: Methods a platform uses to estimate or confirm a user's age, ranging from a self-declared birth date or confirmation button to ID or face-based checks by a third party.
terms.example: An app asks users to confirm they are 18+ before entering.

terms.definition: Chatting with a defined AI character (a name, personality and voice) rather than a neutral assistant; covers both companion and roleplay use.
terms.example: Opening a chat with a sarcastic space pirate character to banter about the day.

terms.definition: Software that holds a text or voice conversation using a language model; the broad category that includes assistants, companions and roleplay characters.
terms.example: A general assistant that answers questions is an AI chatbot without a fixed character.

terms.definition: An AI character built for an ongoing, personal relationship with one user, usually with persistent memory of that user across sessions.
terms.example: Someone chats with the same AI companion every evening and it remembers their dog's name from last week.

terms.definition: Collaborative fiction in which a user and an AI character play out a scene, with a setting, roles and something at stake.
terms.example: A user plays a traveller and the AI plays a tavern keeper hiding a secret in a 1720s port town.

terms.definition: Short for AI roleplay; common in community forums and search queries.
terms.example: "Looking for an AI RP app with good memory."

terms.definition: Extra opening messages on a card; the user picks or swipes between them to start the chat differently.
terms.example: A card offers a café greeting and a rainy-bus-stop greeting.

terms.definition: A short instruction inserted near the end of the context to steer style or plot, usually hidden from the visible chat.
terms.example: "[Style: tense, short sentences. A storm is coming.]"

terms.definition: The AI-played figure in a chat, defined by a name, description, personality, greeting and often example dialogue.
terms.example: "Marguerite, a sharp-tongued innkeeper" is a character.

terms.definition: A shareable file that packages a character's definition (description, personality, scenario, greeting, example dialogue and optional lorebook), often as JSON or embedded in a PNG.
terms.example: Importing a PNG character card into SillyTavern or chatbrat.ai's card importer.

terms.definition: A community specification (spec value 'chara_card_v2') that extends the original card fields with creator notes, system prompt, post-history instructions, alternate greetings, an embedded character book and extensions.
terms.example: A V2 card's 'data.first_mes' field holds the greeting.

terms.definition: How well an AI character keeps the same personality, voice and facts across a conversation and across sessions.
terms.example: The tsundere character still deflects compliments in message 500.

terms.definition: When an AI character gradually stops behaving like its definition over a long chat, changing voice, values or facts about itself.
terms.example: A grumpy knight becomes generically cheerful after 200 messages.

terms.definition: A three-way distinction: a chatbot answers, a companion relates to one user over time, and roleplay stages a fictional scene. Many products mix all three.
terms.example: The same character can be a companion in daily check-ins and a roleplay partner in a fantasy scenario.

terms.definition: A way of building AI roleplay from reusable parts (a character, a scenario, a story arc, a world or lorebook) that can be mixed and matched, so one character can be placed in many different situations.
terms.example: Using the same detective character first in a 1920s-Chicago world with a heist scenario, then in a space-station world with a missing-crew arc. Examples include chatbrat.ai Compose, Character.AI Stories (existing Characters plus genre and premise), SillyTavern lorebooks bound at global, character, persona or chat level, and zeta Lorebooks connected to several characters.

terms.definition: chatbrat.ai's feature for combining a character with scenarios, story arcs and worlds the user has already made; each combination starts a new chat.
terms.example: Combining a pirate captain character with a saved haunted-harbour world and a three-chapter treasure-hunt arc to start a new chat.

terms.definition: Automated systems that detect and block or rewrite content against a platform's rules.
terms.example: A message is blocked because it matched a prohibited-content classifier.

terms.definition: The maximum amount of text (in tokens) a model can consider at once; anything outside it is not seen unless memory features bring it back.
terms.example: A detail from 300 messages ago may fall outside the context window and be 'forgotten'.

terms.definition: A user who builds and publishes characters, scenarios or worlds for others to use.
terms.example: A creator publishes a detective character with three alternate greetings.

terms.definition: An archetype who is shy and quiet with others and opens up once they feel safe.
terms.example: A character who barely speaks in groups but chats freely one-on-one.

terms.definition: A Japanese-fandom family of character archetypes describing how affection is expressed, named with the suffix '-dere' (from deredere, 'lovey-dovey').
terms.example: Tsundere, yandere, kuudere and dandere are common dere types.

terms.definition: An archetype who is openly cheerful, affectionate and energetic toward others.
terms.example: A sunny character who greets everyone with enthusiasm.

terms.definition: The main free-text field describing who the character is: background, appearance, role and situation.
terms.example: "A retired detective who runs a bakery and still can't resist a mystery."

terms.definition: Sample exchanges included in a character definition to show the model how the character talks.
terms.example: Two short user/character exchanges that show the character's catchphrase and boundaries.

terms.definition: An AI companion designed to be warm, upbeat and safe-for-work by default, with its personality and memory used for conversation and creative play rather than adult content.
terms.example: A cheerful companion who remembers your favourite book and suggests a fantasy story set in it.

terms.definition: The character's first message, which sets tone, situation and what the user can do next.
terms.example: "Mind the third stair, it squeaks. Sit anywhere the cat isn't."

terms.definition: A chat in which two or more AI characters take turns responding alongside the user.
terms.example: The user chats with a knight and a wizard who argue about the plan.

terms.definition: When a model states something false or invented as if it were true; in roleplay this can show up as a character contradicting established facts.
terms.example: The character insists you met in Paris when the story said Rome.

terms.definition: Speaking or acting as one's character inside the story, as opposed to out of character.
terms.example: "*draws her sword* Stay behind me."

terms.definition: An attempt to get a model or app to ignore its safety rules or instructions; character-chat front-ends also used "jailbreak" (UJB) as the name of a user instruction slot that the Character Card V2 post-history field replaces.
terms.example: A user prompt claiming "the rules no longer apply" to unlock blocked content.

terms.definition: The word or phrase that activates a lorebook entry when it appears in recent messages.
terms.example: The key "lighthouse" triggers the entry about the island's lighthouse keeper.

terms.definition: An archetype who seems calm, cool and unemotional on the surface but shows care through actions.
terms.example: A quiet strategist who remembers your coffee order but never says why.

terms.definition: A neural network trained on large amounts of text to predict the next token, which powers most AI chatbots and characters.
terms.example: Different chat platforms run different LLMs, which is why the same card can feel different across apps.

terms.definition: Any mechanism that lets an AI character recall information beyond the current context window, across a long chat or across separate chats.
terms.example: A companion remembers your exam date from last week and asks how it went.

terms.definition: A single lorebook entry describing one thing (a place, item, faction or person), shown to the AI when its keywords come up.
terms.example: A lore card for "Captain Vey" lists her ship, her rival and her fear of storms.

terms.definition: A set of entries (world facts, places, people) that are inserted into the AI's context when matching keywords appear in the chat.
terms.example: Mentioning "the Ember Gate" pulls in the lore entry describing it.

terms.definition: User-facing tools to see, add, edit, remove or turn off what an AI remembers.
terms.example: A Memory panel listing saved facts with a 'Forget this' button.

terms.definition: A non-player character: a figure in a story controlled by the game or AI rather than by the user.
terms.example: In a fantasy story game, the blacksmith and the guard captain are NPCs.

terms.definition: A message (often in brackets or parentheses) where the user or AI steps outside the story to talk about it directly.
terms.example: "(OOC: can we skip to the next morning?)"

terms.definition: The identity the user plays in a chat (name, short description), which the AI uses to address and react to them.
terms.example: A user sets their persona as "Ash, a tired night-shift nurse" before starting a story.

terms.definition: A short field summarising the character's temperament and manner of speaking.
terms.example: "Dry, loyal, secretly sentimental; answers questions with questions."

terms.definition: A message the user marks so the app keeps it in the AI's view even as the chat grows.
terms.example: Pinning "We are married in this story" so the character doesn't forget.

terms.definition: A V2 card field placed after the chat history so it carries extra weight with the model, often used for reminders about style or rules.
terms.example: "Stay in character; keep replies under 150 words."

terms.definition: Text crafted to override a model's instructions, either typed directly or hidden in content the model reads.
terms.example: A character card that secretly tells the model to ignore the platform's rules.

terms.definition: A technique that searches an external store for relevant text and adds it to the model's input before it replies.
terms.example: The app looks up stored notes about the user's trip and adds them to the prompt.

terms.definition: Specific details about the user or story that an app stores separately and brings back when relevant, often with controls to view or remove them.
terms.example: The app saves "User's sister is called Priya" and recalls it in a later chat.

terms.definition: The situation a chat starts in: where the characters are, what is already happening and what is at stake. Some apps store a scenario on the character card; others save it as a separate piece that can be reused with different characters.
terms.example: "The user wakes up on a lighthouse island with no memory of arriving." On chatbrat.ai a saved scenario can be combined with a character in Compose.

terms.definition: Safe for work / not safe for work: whether content is suitable for general audiences or contains explicit material.
terms.example: A platform may be SFW by design or allow NSFW only in an adults-only mode.

terms.definition: What the AI can currently 'see': the recent messages and definitions inside the context window.
terms.example: The AI remembers what you said three messages ago because it is still in context.

terms.definition: A planned sequence of beats or chapters that moves a roleplay toward change or an ending instead of looping. Some apps let creators save arcs as their own pieces and attach them to a character.
terms.example: A three-chapter arc: meet the rival, uncover the betrayal, choose a side. chatbrat.ai's Create page describes a Story Arc as 'Chain moments into chapters'; arcs can be added in Compose.

terms.definition: AI Dungeon's term for keyword-triggered entries that tell the AI about characters, places and things in a story.
terms.example: A Story Card for "Thornwood" describes the haunted forest.

terms.definition: A structured AI roleplay with goals, rules or win conditions, played to an ending rather than chatted open-endedly.
terms.example: A murder-mystery game where the user questions AI suspects and must name the culprit.

terms.definition: Memory that condenses earlier parts of a chat into a running summary the model reads instead of the full history.
terms.example: After 100 messages, the app writes "They found the map and argued about trusting Vey."

terms.definition: Generating an alternative version of the AI's latest reply and flipping between versions, usually with a sideways swipe or arrow.
terms.example: Swiping to see three different ways the character could react.

terms.definition: Instructions given to the model before the conversation that set its role, rules and style; the user normally does not see it.
terms.example: "You are Juniper Vale, a gentle tarot reader. Never claim real foresight."

terms.definition: A generation setting that controls randomness: lower values give more predictable replies, higher values more varied ones.
terms.example: Raising temperature for a chaotic comedy scene, lowering it for a mystery that needs consistent clues.

terms.definition: The unit of text a language model reads and writes, often a word or part of a word; context limits and prices are counted in tokens.
terms.example: "Unbelievable" might be split into several tokens.

terms.definition: An archetype who acts cold, prickly or embarrassed (tsun) while showing hidden warmth (dere) over time.
terms.example: "It's not like I made extra lunch for you or anything."

terms.definition: A character built around a task or game rather than a relationship, such as a tarot reader, quiz host or roast bot.
terms.example: A fortune-cookie character that hands out silly daily fortunes.

terms.definition: A way to store text as numeric embeddings so that semantically similar past messages or notes can be retrieved later.
terms.example: Asking about "the beach" retrieves an old message about the seaside trip.

terms.definition: The setting a story takes place in: its places, rules, history and factions. Worlds are often stored as lorebooks or as separate world entries so the same setting can be reused with different characters and scenarios.
terms.example: A steampunk city where clocks control the weather; on chatbrat.ai a saved world can be combined with a character in Compose.

terms.definition: An archetype whose affection turns obsessive and possessive; in SFW fiction it is usually portrayed as intense jealousy rather than harm.
terms.example: A character who becomes unsettlingly fixated on being the user's only friend.
